libc_exec/015-strchr-strstr.c.rationale: `strpbrk(h, "yx") - h` for h = "abcabcabcdabcde-xyzzy" (the last of the program's twelve printed values). Pristine upstream c3ff8c53f prints 17 (verbatim stdout `2 21 10 0 9 9 18 15 1 9 15 17`); gcc 13 with glibc prints 16, the index of the first 'x'. Mechanism (tray 20, the macro-type rank defect inside the shared C library): musl's strcspn builds its byte set with `if (!BITOP(byteset, *c, |=)) break;` and `!` on the size_t value is elaborated as `== 0` under the usual arithmetic conversions of (size_t, int), which upstream's rank table narrows to unsigned int -- `(size_t)1 << 57` compares equal to 0 -- so the set-building loop stops after the set's FIRST character and "yx" becomes {y}; the fork, whose rank functions normalise the macro types through the implementation's alias table (fork-ahead delta of 2026-11-04, [USER 2026-11-04]), prints 16 = gcc. Class shared-model-fix; the row leaves when upstream absorbs the fix.
